entries.1:1: The writer, a church leader, is writing to a dear friend named Gaius, whom he genuinely loves. It shows that faith creates real, warm friendships worth naming and honoring.
entries.1:2: He prays that Gaius will do well and stay healthy, just as his spiritual life is already strong. It's a reminder that caring for someone's whole well-being, body and soul, is a good and loving prayer.
entries.1:3: He was thrilled when visitors reported that Gaius believes the truth and lives it out. It's encouraging to know that faithful living brings joy to the people who care about you.
entries.1:4: Nothing makes him happier than hearing that the people he has guided are living faithfully. For anyone who mentors others, this is the deepest kind of joy.
entries.1:5: He praises Gaius for kindly welcoming traveling believers he didn't even know. Being generous to strangers who share your faith is a real good work.
entries.1:6: These travelers told the church how much Gaius loved them, and the writer urges him to keep helping them on their way properly. Supporting people who serve God is the right thing to do.
entries.1:7: These workers went out to spread the message about God's name and refused to take money from people outside the faith. Their commitment shows real dedication, and it puts the responsibility on believers to support them.
entries.1:8: So we should welcome and support people like them, because that makes us partners in their work for the faith. Even simple hospitality makes you part of something bigger.
entries.1:9: He wrote to the church, but a man named Diotrephes, who loves being in charge, refuses to accept his authority. It's a warning that pride and a hunger for control can block what God is doing.
entries.1:10: If he comes, he'll confront Diotrephes for spreading nasty rumors, refusing to host the traveling believers, and even kicking out of the church anyone who does welcome them. It shows how one power-hungry person can hurt a whole community.
entries.1:11: He tells his friend not to imitate evil but good, because doing good shows you belong to God, while doing evil shows you don't really know him. What you copy shapes who you are.
entries.1:12: Everyone speaks well of Demetrius, and the truth itself backs that up, with the writer adding his own good word. A good reputation built on honest living is worth trusting.
entries.1:13: He has a lot more to say but doesn't want to write it all down. Some things are better said than written.
entries.1:14: He hopes to visit soon and talk in person. Face-to-face time matters more than letters for building real relationships.
